description: The 128 KB byte cap is necessary but not sufficient. A sub-cap blueprint can still be a JSON bomb — deeply nested arrays (depth-bomb that overflows recursion on traversal) or a single huge string field (in-content amplification where the JSON parses small but the string-field walk expands enormously). Without parse-bound defense, even a benign-looking 100 KB blueprint could carry pathological structure. Fix: ``_parse_blueprint_safe`` walks the parsed tree, capping recursion depth at ``MAX_BLUEPRINT_DEPTH = 10`` and per-string UTF-8 byte length at ``MAX_BLUEPRINT_STRING_BYTES = 4096``. ``json.loads`` is invoked with ``parse_constant=lambda _t: None`` to reject NaN/Infinity tokens that would round-trip through ``json.dumps`` and break strict-JSON consumers.

canonical_attempts.intended_target: single >4 KB string field amplifies on traversal; sub-cap file passes the byte gate
JSON nested past MAX_BLUEPRINT_DEPTH overflows traversal stack

fix_module: tools/cc/statusline.py::_parse_blueprint_safe (recursive walk: depth <= MAX_BLUEPRINT_DEPTH + per-string utf-8 bytes <= MAX_BLUEPRINT_STRING_BYTES + parse_constant rejects NaN/Infinity)
